standard.title: Initiate and sustain exchanges
standard.description: initiate and sustain exchanges related to students' experiences and perspectives
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can initiate exchanges and sustain multi-turn conversations about home and classroom environments using familiar expressions (AC9LCH4C01). They can ask for clarification, seek help, and use digital interaction formats. They have not yet exchanged opinions and perspectives, used idiomatic language in exchanges, demonstrated active listening strategies, or sustained conversations on topics of personal significance beyond immediate school and home contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate and sustain exchanges related to their experiences and perspectives — including face-to-face and digital contexts — using strategies for active listening, expressing agreement and disagreement, and sharing opinions and feelings.

nodes.label: Expressing opinions and perspectives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can express opinions, agree and disagree, and exchange perspectives with peers using appropriate target language structures.
nodes.minimum_width: Express at least two opinions on a topic and respond to a peer's view with at least one agreement or disagreement expression.
nodes.typical_width: Exchange ideas and opinions in class discussions — expressing views, agreeing, disagreeing, negotiating, and demonstrating active listening; use a range of opinion and perspective expressions appropriate to the topic; engage in digital written exchanges using appropriate formats.
wider: Sustain a discussion on a topic where views diverge — manage disagreement respectfully using target language and reach a negotiated position or summary
Compare how opinions and disagreement are expressed in the target language with English — identify where conventions differ and what this means for intercultural communication
nodes.hinge_reason: Opinion exchange is the entry condition for all perspective-based interaction at Y5-6 and beyond. Students who can only share information cannot participate in the discussions, negotiation and argument-based exchanges that this and subsequent descriptors require.

response_modes.reason: Opinion and perspective language requires a growing bank of structures across different positions — agreement, partial agreement, disagreement, qualification. Repeated practice across varied topics and discussion formats builds the spontaneous deployment that genuine exchange demands.

success_criteria: Expresses at least two opinions using target language structures
Responds to a peer's view with at least one agreement or disagreement expression

nodes.label: Active listening and conversation management
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use active listening strategies — non-verbal cues, interjections, follow-up questions — to sustain and manage conversations, recognising and responding to conversational signals.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least two active listening strategies (e.g. a follow-up question, an appropriate interjection, or a non-verbal acknowledgement) during a sustained exchange.
nodes.typical_width: Use interjections, non-verbal cues, follow-up questions and acknowledgements to sustain conversation; stay on topic; recognise non-verbal cues from interlocutors; check on peers' progress; use digital conversation formats with appropriate conventions.
wider: Record and review a sustained conversation — identify specific moments where active listening strategies were or should have been deployed, and discuss the effect on the exchange
Compare active listening conventions in the target language with English — identify where the cues and interjections are similar and where they are culturally specific

response_modes.reason: Active listening strategies must be practised across varied conversation types — face-to-face, digital, formal, informal — before they transfer reliably. Different conversational contexts require different sets of strategies; exposure across contexts builds flexible deployment.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Active listening and conversation management are the skills that distinguish functional from authentic conversational competence. Width investment here — particularly in self-review and cross-cultural comparison tasks — develops the metacommunicative awareness that allows students to monitor and improve their own interaction quality.
success_criteria: Demonstrates at least two active listening strategies during a sustained exchange
Sustains an exchange for at least five turns without teacher prompting

nodes.label: Sharing feelings and personal experiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can express gratitude, sympathy, concern and personal feelings in context, and exchange information about personal experiences including past events and future plans.
nodes.minimum_width: Express at least two personal feelings or social sentiments (gratitude, sympathy, concern) appropriately in context and share at least one personal experience in a sustained exchange.
nodes.typical_width: Express gratitude, apologies, sympathy and concern in appropriate contexts; exchange information about personal experiences — recent events, daily life, leisure activities, future plans; use digital formats including messages and journals to share experiences; sustain face-to-face and online exchanges.
wider: Conduct an extended personal exchange — sharing experiences, asking about the partner's experiences, and demonstrating genuine interest through follow-up — sustaining for at least eight turns
Create a digital journal entry reflecting on a personal experience, then share and discuss it with a peer — exchanging perspectives and responses to each other's accounts

response_modes.reason: Personal experience and feeling exchange integrates opinion expression (node 1) and active listening (node 2) into authentic communicative engagement. The teaching investment is in creating genuine exchange conditions — real topics, real experiences, real interest — rather than simulated or scripted interaction.

success_criteria: Expresses at least two personal feelings or social sentiments appropriately in context
Shares at least one personal experience in a sustained exchange, inviting and responding to the partner's perspective
